newsitem.title: BRAZIL: SOCCER-URUGUAY TURN TO FRANCESCOLI IN QUEST FOR WIN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-URUGUAY TURN TO FRANCESCOLI IN QUEST FOR WIN.

text.p: Uruguay have turned to midfielder Enzo Francescoli, who celebrates his 35th birthday next month, in an attempt to revitalise their team for Tuesday's crucial World Cup qualifying match against Bolivia.

The once mighty Uruguayans failed to qualify for the last World Cup finals and find themselves in danger of missing out again after two defeats -- one at home to Paraguay -- and a draw in their last three qualifying matches.

Francescoli, a survivor of the 1986 World Cup in which Uruguay reached the second round, had announced his retirement from international soccer after his country won the Copa America, which they hosted, last year.
But after numerous requests from increasingly beleaguered coach Hector Nunez, Francescoli, who plays his club soccer in Argentina for River Plate, has changed his mind.
Bolivia, who edged out Uruguay in 1994, have several selection problems.

Marco Etcheverry, who usually pulls the strings in midfield, is suspended after receiving two yellow cards and top striker Erwin Sanchez is out of action for the rest of the year with a long-term injury suffered playing for his Portuguese club Boavista.
Full-back Miguel Rimba and midfielder Ivan Castillo were last week added to the injury list.
Bolivia themselves have not had the greatest of starts and sacked coach Dusan Draskevic after last month's disappointing 0-0 draw at home to Peru.
Spaniard Antonio Lopes, who coached the team until last year, has been brought back in a move which highlights the topsy-turvy world of South American soccer coaching.
Rivalry between the two teams has become ever more intense, particularly after Uruguay led an unsuccesful campaign to have Bolivia's high-altitude capital La Paz banned from staging matches.
The top four of the South American nations, who have been thrown into one huge qualfying group and play each other home and away, will play in France in 1998.
Argentina, another traditional power also in a sticky situation, are away to minnows Venezuela in one of three matches to be played Wednesday.
Coach Daniel Passarella knows his team dare not lose after being held to a draw at home by Paraguay last month in a game which saw goalkeeper Jose Luis Chilavert score for Paraguay from a free kick.
The result came on top of defeat away to Ecuador and a lucky draw away to Peru.
Venezuela have lost all previous seven encounters with Argentina, many by large scores.
Group leaders Colombia, with midfielders Freddy Rincon and Leonel Alvarez back after suspension, face their old master Francisco Maturana when they play away to Ecuador.

Maturana led his country from soccer obscurity to two successive World Cups but then abandoned the job in the wake of death threats and failure in the 1994 competition and moved south to Colombia's smaller and calmer neighbour.
Ecuador have never played in the World Cup finals but are second to Colombia after winning three of their four first games.

Paraguay, looking to qualify for the first time since 1986, play for the first time in their intimidating Defensores del Chaco stadium when they take on Chile, a team with a notoriously leaky defence.
Peru do not play this week while Brazil are exempt from the qualifying marathon as champions.
